title: Enforce environment-bound token lifecycles with fingerprinting, rotation alarms, and audit markers
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Problem: We currently allow service and user API keys that can be reused across environments without clear provenance. This causes confused ownership, noisy audit trails, and risky long-lived keys that bypass RBAC v2 intent. Goal: Build a token lifecycle enforcement layer that ties API keys to environment fingerprints (hosted/dedicated/private), enforces expiration/rotation rules by scope, emits structured audit markers, and raises rotation alarms when grace windows are approaching. This ticket covers the core runtime + control-plane changes needed to ensure keys are environment-bound and observable.

Scope:
- Token metadata: attach immutable environment_fingerprint and human-friendly naming convention at creation.
- Expiry & rotation: support per-scope TTLs, configurable grace windows, and automated rotation reminders.
- Audit markers: emit structured audit events for create/rotate/revoke with fingerprint and requester_identity fields.
- Enforcement: runtime checks that reject tokens used outside their bound environment unless explicitly allowlisted.
- Admin UI: console surface to see token health, upcoming expirations, and one-click rotate/revoke.

Non-Goals: cross-account token federation, full key escrow/recovery, and multi-tenant policy engine (covered in RBAC v2 core tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Token create API attaches an immutable environment_fingerprint and user-supplied name that follows agreed naming convention.
Runtime rejects token usage if environment_fingerprint mismatch and no allowlist entry exists; appropriate 401/403 error codes returned.
Audit log entries created for create/rotate/revoke operations containing token_key, environment_fingerprint, requester_identity, and rotation_reason.
Console shows token list with upcoming expirations, color-coded alarm thresholds, and a rotate button that triggers server-side rotation flow.
Rotation alarm system sends email/pager alerts to owners when grace window <= configured threshold and is configurable per-project.
Unit and integration tests cover enforcement, metadata propagation, and audit event schema compatibility.
decisions: Use an environment_fingerprint (sha256 of region+deployment_id+cluster_id) as immutable token metadata rather than embedding raw env ids to reduce surface for accidental leakage.

Implement enforcement in the serving runtime for the fast-fail path and in API gateway for early rejection; logs will be produced from both layers but canonical audit events produced by the control plane.
Rotation alarms are configurable per-project; default grace window = 14 days and alarm threshold = 7 days. We’ll expose these as project-level settings in the Console.
Naming convention: <team>-<purpose>-<env>-<short-hash> (example: infra-ingest-prod-5f2a). We decided against including user emails in names for privacy and search noise reasons.
blockers: Final schema approval for audit events from observability team (ticket OBS-1123).
RBAC v2 role for token owners needs completion (parent ticket: ENG-79210).
KMS integration for rotation flow needs production keys available in dedicated test clusters.

notes: Trade-offs: strong environment binding improves security posture but adds operational friction for legitimate cross-environment workflows. We will provide allowlist APIs and short-lived cross-env tokens for service-to-service calls with explicit approval. The enforcement uses a layered approach to keep latency impact minimal: API gateway rejects most mismatches; runtime acts as last line of defense.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Control plane - persist env_fp on token create, implement naming convention, and emit audit events (2 sprints).
Phase 2: Runtime/API gateway - add env_fp validation and error codes, performance test across typical token lookup paths (2 sprints).
Phase 3: Console & Alerts - surface expirations, alarms, and rotate flow (1 sprint).
Phase 4: Rollout - feature-flagged beta for 10% of orgs, gather metrics on false positives, iterate (2 weeks).
